text: The agent-authority part is held inside the two operations the service already publishes: POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise and GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session on the base /api/recovery/access/v1, with the caller type AGENT, the agent code, the case, the trigger event, the policy version, the autonomy mode, the capability area, the right and the field IDs on the request, and admitted, reasonCode, roleCodes, roleClass, scope, capabilityArea, right, letters, matrixVersion, maskingVersion, policyVersion, autonomyMode and fieldMarkers on the answer. The consumed reference-data and parameters reads of rwb-case sit on that service's base through their client libraries.
why: No source names the agent-authority part or its element names, while the legacy story needs the answer and the service already publishes the authorise operation and the session read; the base and path rule are DP-13 and the naming rules of the context pack, and the answer is composed from the rows and lists TSD P4 v3 T3.1, T3.2 and T6.1 already define.
read: RWB-E1-062 sections 4, 10, 12 and 17; TSD P4 v3 T-A.2 API-P4-012, T3.1, T3.2 and T6.1; Architecture v5 slide 14; context pack P4 (service row and naming rules); Template and Rules section R4 and DP-13
confirm: Solution architect, P4 and the API specification owner at the wave 1 contract review
impact: If the element names or the part differ, the contract document, the two REST tables and the fakes change; the row reads, the default-deny rule and the one-entry-per-answer rule are unchanged.

text: A refusal carries exactly one of three reason codes: CALLER_KIND when the subject does not resolve to a role of class NON_HUMAN_ACTOR, RIGHT_NOT_HELD when the letter asked is absent in the area asked, and SCOPE_NOT_ALL when the subject's default scope is narrower than ALL. Each answers 403 with MSG-P4-002 and the reason code; a missing member or a value outside its list answers 422 with MSG-GEN-001; an entry that cannot be written answers 503 with MSG-P7-003.
why: The legacy and the FSD fix only 403 with MSG-P4-002, and the three refusal causes have different consequences for the caller; the story needs a legible, stable code per cause and cannot read it from any source.
read: RWB-E1-062 section 5 X7 and section 14 MSG-P4-002; FSD P4 v3 A2.4 VR-P4-004-1, AC-EXC-P4-004-01 and AC-ALT-P4-004-02; TSD P4 v3 T6.2; FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-007-03 for the 503 shape
confirm: Solution architect, P4 and the security administrator role
impact: A different code set changes the enumeration of the contract and the assertions of AC2 and AC4 only; the statuses and the messages are the legacy ones and do not move.

text: For the screening run the personal fields are the two the legacy marks masked - DF-INT-011 (the ledger summary) and DF-DOC-015 (the stored document field value) - together with the party identifiers a case read presents, and they are answered masked for a non-human actor at the masking version in force, with the shapes the FSD fixes for a screen: XXXXXXXXX1234, XXXXXX5678 and XXXX-XX-XX. A field ID with no masking_rule row is masked, and no clear value, rendering or last four digits is answered.
why: The legacy names two masked fields and no format for an agent, and the masking answer is default deny by role and field; the two legacy fields and the FSD shapes are the only values a source gives, and the rest is a decision that must be visible as one.
read: RWB-E1-062 section 11 and section 17; FSD P4 v3 A2.5, AC-ALT-P4-004-01 and AC-EXC-P4-004-05; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 masking_rule and T7 NFR-039 and NFR-040
applied_in: 2 Business rationale; 3 Preconditions; 7 AC5; 8 BR5; 11 Data; 13
confirm: Compliance and PDPA officer with the security administrator role
impact: A wider or narrower field list is a masking version and changes no build, by the feature rule of BR5 and the build check of AC7.

text: The service identity of the agent platform holds default scope ALL for this key, so a screening run is not restricted by team or region; a role whose scope is OWN, TEAM or REGION is refused with SCOPE_NOT_ALL rather than resolved, because no table of rwb_access binds a role to a list of teams or regions.
why: The shadow sample of 200 cases spans every team and region and no source states the scope of a non-human role, while role.default_scope is a required column that must hold one of the four list values.
read: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 role.default_scope, T3.2 LOV-SCOPE and T6.1; FSD P4 v3 A2.14; RWB-E1-062 sections 4 and 10
applied_in: 3 Preconditions; 5 Exception paths X6; 7 AC1; 8 BR4; 10 Authority
confirm: Security administrator role in the matrix version in force
impact: A narrower scope on the identity would stop every run outside its team and turn AC1 into a refusal; the code path is the same and the change is one row of the matrix.

text: The access entry of an agent answer carries the actor, the caller type, the agent code, the policy version, the autonomy mode, the case, the trigger event, the field IDs with their markers, the matrix version, the masking version and the time, with decision code AC-READ for an admission and AC-DENY for a refusal, in the append-only chain written by RWB-P4-E1039-APP.
why: The FSD fixes the entry of a screen read and of a refusal and says every read is logged, but no source names the members of a read by a service identity; the members chosen are the ones an audit of a shadow run needs, and the two decision codes are the FSD's own.
read: FSD P4 v3 A2.7, A2.8, AC-P4-007-01, AC-ALT-P4-007-02 and AC-EXC-P4-007-04; TSD P4 v3 T6.2 and T7 NFR-042; RWB-E1-062 section 10
confirm: Internal audit role with the writer of RWB-P4-E1039-APP
impact: A different member list changes the entry mapper, the query of AC6 and the register of the access log; the decision codes and the chain stay as the FSD fixes them.

text: The H and C rows of the DP table for DP-04, DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-15, DP-19 and DP-20 are already build dependencies of the service baseline and of the platform, so this secondary slice adds none of its own: metadata 'Depends on (build)' stays None and 'Contract dependencies' stays RWB-P10-E1062-CON, and the story builds from Day 1 against the published contracts and their fakes.
why: The WP fixes H as empty and C as the agent contract of the key, while the DP table names the platform contract stories of the patterns applied; the contradiction is resolved by the service baseline, which already carries those libraries.
read: Template and Rules section R5.5 and R5.7; the WP metadata for RWB-P4-E1062-APP; RWB-P4-E1037-CON and the service baseline
confirm: Delivery lead at the wave 1 build-sequence review
impact: If the baseline does not carry a library, that library becomes an H dependency of the service and not of this slice; no criterion changes.
